title: The Mothership LLC operating agreement, draft dated March 20, 2016
authors: The Mothership LLC; shared by the Federation of Egalitarian Communities
publication: Federation of Egalitarian Communities, Systems & Structures
access_status: complete public HTML transcription of an explicitly labelled draft instrument inspected; placeholder signature pages mean execution and adoption are not established
evidence_scope: draft withdrawal, member-record access, leaving-fund reserve, retirement-fund disbursement, debt priority, mediation, and arbitration terms
sequence_allegation: a member may withdraw for any or no reason on 30 days' written notice; the same leaving-fund payout applies after expulsion
sequence_assessment: member access to books and internally prepared reports; pre-existing assets and liabilities disclosed and transferred in title or trust as member consensus decides; no independent valuation or former-member record right is specified
sequence_intervention: Leaving Fund payable within two business days with cash reserved for all members; a distinct retirement fund may be paid over ten years or at a 50 percent lump-sum value
sequence_review: negotiation, mutually acceptable mediation, then arbitration; parties initially bear their own expenses and share neutral costs, while community coverage depends on member consensus
sequence_later_outcome: no signed final agreement, actual reserve balance, withdrawal, expulsion, payout, dispute, housing transition, or later member outcome was located
notes: The document is a primary draft with sample names and blank signatures, not evidence of implementation or a validated model. Moora Moora's public manifesto was also inspected as a lead comparator but expressly says its figures are not current and directs readers to nonpublic formal rules

lane: adjacent pooled-health governance and claim account
title: PEACH official governance page and administrator claim account
authors: Federation of Egalitarian Communities; Laird Schaub interviewed by Mira Luna
publication: Federation of Egalitarian Communities; Grassroots Economic Organizing
access_status: current official organization page plus a 2013 first-person administrator interview inspected; governing rules, claim forms, claim ledger, audits, and legal-status record were not public in the inspected materials
evidence_scope: community-level governance, contribution and reimbursement mechanics, a historical claim-payment assertion, reserve investment, participating-community withdrawal, and the express absence of an individual entitlement
sequence_allegation: a participating community incurs and approves a member's medical expense; the 2013 account says claims are made by communities rather than individuals
sequence_assessment: the community pays first and decides whether to file; the 2013 account reports a licensed-provider prescription condition for treatments, but no individual independent intake, denial notice, hardship, or appeal process
sequence_intervention: historical account: PEACH reimburses 90 percent above a $5,000 community-paid threshold up to a formula-based annual limit; a withdrawing community receives 90 percent of contributions less reimbursements
sequence_review: one representative from each participating community governs PEACH separately from FEC delegates, with a technical administrator; no public member-level appeal or external review route was located
sequence_later_outcome: the 2013 interview claimed roughly one claim per year for about 200 people in eight communities and all claims paid except one; the current official page supplies no audit, denial denominator, current reserve, or later individual outcome
notes: The sources' self-insurance terminology is descriptive, not an independent legal conclusion. The official page corroborates the governance layer but not the 2013 claim history. No treatment choice, coverage waiver, or private-community medical authority is recommended

lane: adjacent Hutterite allocation and planned-fission record
title: Walter Estate v. Walter and the Hutterian Brethren public Daughter Colony record
authors: Alberta Court of Appeal; Hutterites.org member editors
access_status: reported appellate judgment text and the official member-managed Hutterites.org description inspected; the 1972 trust agreement, trial judgment, and a specific planned-division schedule were not obtained
evidence_scope: a primary court allocation after Felger Colony partnership dissolution, kept distinct from the current Hutterite public description of customary daughter-colony formation
sequence_allegation: Walter concerned dissolution and competing beneficiary interests after loss of communal purpose; the public daughter-colony record describes a planned scale response near 30 families or 150 people
sequence_assessment: the trial court identified nine partners and assessed interests by service, with an offset for diverted funds; in a planned split, assets are valued into home- and daughter-colony portions while people may volunteer or be divided into groups
sequence_intervention: the appellate court affirmed the service-based allocation; the public planned-fission account describes volunteer relocation or selection between groups by lot, followed by a rapid family move in some branches
sequence_review: court appeal for the dissolution allocation; no independent appeal, dissent process, or neutral valuation route is described on the daughter-colony page
sequence_later_outcome: the legal record reports the allocation judgment, not member wellbeing or successor viability; the public planned-fission account reports aggregate structure and acknowledges pain but no comparative later outcome
notes: A 2021 open-access field study corroborates inventory, valuation, debt division, and later financial strain and describes a 1966 James Valley accounting, but the accounting itself was not directly accessible. Neither aggregate parity nor lot-casting establishes individual consent

title: Schedule 1A – the Notice under the High Court order of July 25, 2025, with current JFCT closure phases
authors: High Court of Justice; Jesus Fellowship Community Trust trustees
access_status: complete four-page official notice, official closure-phase page, August 2025 update, and March 2026 update inspected; the full order and complete Trust Deed were available only on request in the inspected notice and were not obtained
evidence_scope: court-supervised claim cut-off before trust-asset distribution plus current trust-deed-based historic-request and residual-apportionment rules
sequence_allegation: claims outside the Trust Deed and listed-beneficiary position had to be notified with identity, facts, legal basis, evidence, and amount or calculation by October 16, 2025
sequence_assessment: trustees classify notified claims as rejected or pending resolution under the order; historic and apportionment eligibility separately depends on records, defined contribution periods, deadlines, and beneficiary votes
sequence_intervention: the court procedure preserves timely notified claims before distribution; separate phases cover initial transition payments, redress and claims, historic requests, and residual apportionment
sequence_review: High Court order and potential litigation for court-notice claims; Trust Deed and listed-beneficiary votes control later discretionary phases; legal advice and litigation costs for notice claims fall on claimants
sequence_later_outcome: the trustees declared the court claims procedure complete on January 23, 2026; March 2026 deed amendments added two Phase 3 categories whose registration window closed April 30, 2026; final distributions, closure, and recipient outcomes remain incomplete
notes: A claims cut-off, redress award, beneficiary vote, or completed trust distribution is not a fair-exit outcome by itself. The public notice says untimely covered claims become permanently unavailable and that claimants bear their own legal costs; the record does not establish accessibility, family repair, or later wellbeing
